I implemented `parse_amount(text)` in `ledgerly/importers.py`.

**What it does:**
- Strips surrounding whitespace
- Removes an optional leading `$`
- Accepts thousands separators (e.g. `1,234.50`)
- Returns a `Decimal` (money stays Decimal end-to-end, per note at-0009)
- Rejects invalid input, negatives, and amounts with more than two decimal places by raising `BillingError("invalid_amount", ...)` (per note at-0003)
- Uses a private `_parse` helper to keep the public function short (per note at-c0188)

All 10 tests pass, and I verified edge cases including `"$1,234.50"`, `" 12 "`, `"0.00"`, and rejection of `"-1"`, `"1.234"`, `"1,23"`, `"abc"`, and non-string inputs.
